n40463.content:
\begin{proof}
Denote by $\mathcal{N}_{n}$ the set of all matrices in $M_{n, n+1}(\mathbb{K})$ having the rank equal to
$n$. For every $M \in\mathcal{N}_{n}$ the dimension of the vector space $N(M) < \mathbb{K}^{n+1}$ equals
$1$ by the rank–nullity theorem, so
$(N(M)\setminus\left\lbrace \theta\right\rbrace)_{\sim} \in \mathbb{P}^{n}(\mathbb{K})$.
We thus have the map
 \[\begin{array}{c}
 \mathcal{N}_{n} \to \mathbb{P}^{n}(\mathbb{K})\\
 M \mapsto (N(M)\setminus\left\lbrace \theta\right\rbrace)_{\sim}
 \end{array}\]
Since matrices of the same size have equal null spaces if and only if they are row equivalent,
the induced map
\[
  \mathcal{N}_{n} / GL_{n}(\mathbb{K})  \to \mathbb{P}^{n}(\mathbb{K})
\]
is well-defined and injective. It is also surjective, since every vector subspace of $\mathbb{K}^{n+1}$
having dimension equal to $1$ is the null space of a matrix in $\mathcal{N}_{n}$.

Since the canonical map
\[
\mathcal{M}_{n}  \to \mathcal{N}_{n}/GL_{n}(\mathbb{K})
\]
is bijective, the lemma follows.
\end{proof}

n40464.title: Proof of Theorem \ref{theorem-1}
n40464.content:
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem \ref{theorem-1}]
\leanok
\uses{lemma-5}
\proves{theorem-1}
It is enough to prove the statement for $k=n+1$ since we may apply induction.

Denote
\[S=\left\lbrace
[f_{1}(x) \colon  \ldots \colon  f_{n+1}(x)] \colon x \in X \setminus \mathrm{Z}(f_{1}, \ldots, f_{n+1})
\right\rbrace. \]
By Lemma \ref{lemma-5} every element $s$ of $S$ defines a unique matrix in $\mathcal{M}_{n}$;
denote this matrix by $M_{s}$. Examine the set
\[T=\mathcal{M}_{n}\setminus \left\lbrace M_{s} \colon s \in S \right\rbrace. \]
By Lemma \ref{lemma-5} the number of elements in $\mathcal{M}_{n}$ equals the cardinality of
$\mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})$, i.e., $\frac{q^{n+1}-1}{q-1}$. The number of elements in $S$ is at most
the cardinality of $X$, i.e., $\frac{q^{n+1}-q}{q-1}$. Hence the cardinality of $T$ is at least
$\frac{q^{n+1}-1}{q-1}-\frac{q^{n+1}-q}{q-1}=1$. So choose a matrix $M\in T$. Our
$g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n}$ are defined by
\[\left[ \begin{array}{c}
g_{1}\\
\vdots\\
g_{n}
\end{array}\right]=M \left[ \begin{array}{c}
f_{1}\\
\vdots\\
f_{n+1}
\end{array}\right].\]
Indeed, the inclusion $\mathrm{Z}(f_{1}, \ldots, f_{n+1}) \subset \mathrm{Z}(g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n})$
is obvious, and by the definition of $T$ the set $\mathrm{Z}(g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n})$ is disjoint
from $X \setminus \mathrm{Z}(f_{1}, \ldots, f_{n+1})$, i.e.,
$\mathrm{Z}(g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n}) \subset \mathrm{Z}(f_{1}, \ldots, f_{n+1})$.
\end{proof}

n40466.content:
\begin{proof}
\leanok
\proves{lemma-6}
Denote by $I_{r, k, l}$ the matrix in $M_{k, l}(\mathbb{K})$ having $x_{11}=\ldots=x_{rr}=1$ and all
remaining entries equal to 0. Denote the rank of $A$ by $r$. Let $G_{1} \in GL_{n}(\mathbb{K})$ and
$G_{2} \in GL_{m}(\mathbb{K})$ be matrices transforming $A$ into $I_{r, n, m}$, i.e.,
$G_{1} A G_{2} = I_{r, n, m}$. Since $I_{r, n, m}=I_{r, n, n}I_{n, n, m}$, we get
$A=G_{1}^{-1}I_{r, n, n}I_{n, n, m}G_{2}^{-1}$. Let $G_{3} \in GL_{n}(\mathbb{K})$ be the matrix
transforming $I_{n, n, m}G_{2}^{-1}$ into reduced row echelon form. We have
\[A=G_{1}^{-1}I_{r, n, n}G_{3}^{-1} G_{3}^{}I_{n, n, m}G_{2}^{-1}.\]
Put $B=G_{1}^{-1}I_{r, n, n}G_{3}^{-1}$ and $M= G_{3}^{}I_{n, n, m}G_{2}^{-1}$.
\end{proof}

n40467.title: Proof of Proposition \ref{prop-2}
n40467.content:
\begin{proof}[Proof of Proposition \ref{prop-2}]
\leanok
\uses{lemma-5,lemma-6}
\proves{prop-2}
For every point $P \in \mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})$ choose a set of homogeneous coordinates for $P$ and
denote it by $c_{P}$. Define $X_{n}=\left\lbrace c_{P} \colon P \in \mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}}) \right\rbrace$.
The cardinality of $X_{n}$ is $\frac{q^{n+1}-1}{q-1}=\frac{q^{n+1}-q}{q-1}+1$. Consider
$f_{1}, \ldots, f_{n+1} \in \mathrm{Map}(X_{n},{\mathbb{F}_{q}})$ defined in the following way: for every
$x\in X_{n}$ put
\[f_{i}(x) = \text{the } i\text{th coordinate of } x.\]
We have $\mathrm{Z}(f_{1}, \ldots, f_{n+1})=\emptyset$.

Let $g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n} \in \mathrm{Span}(f_{1}, \ldots, f_{n+1})$, i.e.,
\[\left[ \begin{array}{c}
g_{1}\\
\vdots\\
g_{n}
\end{array}\right]=A \left[ \begin{array}{c}
f_{1}\\
\vdots\\
f_{n+1}
\end{array}\right]\]
for some matrix $A \in M_{n, n+1}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})$.
By Lemma \ref{lemma-6} there exist a matrix $M \in M_{n, n+1}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})$ in reduced row echelon form
having the rank equal to $n$, and a matrix $B \in M_{n, n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})$ such that $A=BM$. Hence by
Lemma \ref{lemma-5} we get that there is $x \in X_{n}$ belonging to
$\mathrm{Z}(g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n})$.
\end{proof}

n40470.title: Proof of Corollary \ref{corollary-4}
n40470.content:
\begin{proof}[Proof of Corollary \ref{corollary-4}]
\leanok
\proves{corollary-4}
\uses{theorem-1}
Let $\left\lbrace f_{1}, \ldots, f_{k}\right\rbrace $ be the image via $\phi$ of a subset of
$\mathcal{F}$. Let $\alpha \in \mathrm{Z}(f_{1}, \ldots, f_{k})$. Denote by
$\bar{f_{1}}, \ldots, \bar{f_{k}}$ the images of $f_{1}, \ldots, f_{k}$ via the restriction
homomorphism
\[\begin{array}{c}
  r \colon \mathrm{Map}(\mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}}),{\mathbb{F}_{q}}) \to
    \mathrm{Map}(\mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})\setminus\left\lbrace \alpha\right\rbrace,{\mathbb{F}_{q}})\\
  r(f)=f |_{\mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})\setminus\left\lbrace \alpha\right\rbrace}.
\end{array}\]
For any positive integer $n$ we have
\[\left| \mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})\setminus\left\lbrace \alpha\right\rbrace\right|
  =\left| \mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})\right| -1 = \frac{q^{n+1}-1}{q-1}-1= \frac{q^{n+1}-q}{q-1}.\]
So we apply Theorem \ref{theorem-1} to get
$\bar{g_{1}}, \ldots, \bar{g_{n}}\in \mathrm{Span}(\bar{f_{1}}, \ldots, \bar{f_{k}})$
such that $\mathrm{Z}(\bar{g_{1}}, \ldots, \bar{g_{n}}) =\mathrm{Z}(\bar{f_{1}}, \ldots, \bar{f_{k}})$.
Let $A \in M_{k, n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}})$ be such that
\[\left[ \begin{array}{c}
  \bar{g_{1}}\\
  \vdots\\
  \bar{g_{n}}
\end{array}\right]=A \left[ \begin{array}{c}
  \bar{f_{1}}\\
  \vdots\\
  \bar{f_{k}}
\end{array}\right].\]
Define $g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n} \in \mathrm{Map}(\mathbb{P}^{n}({\mathbb{F}_{q}}),{\mathbb{F}_{q}})$ by
\[\left[ \begin{array}{c}
  {g_{1}}\\
  \vdots\\
  {g_{n}}
\end{array}\right]=A \left[ \begin{array}{c}
  {f_{1}}\\
  \vdots\\
  {f_{k}}
\end{array}\right].\]
We are done, since
\[\begin{array}{l}
  \mathrm{Z}(f_{1}, \ldots, f_{k})= \left\lbrace \alpha\right\rbrace \cup
    \mathrm{Z}(\bar{f_{1}}, \ldots, \bar{f_{k}}),  \, \mathrm{and}\\
  \mathrm{Z}(g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n})= \left\lbrace \alpha\right\rbrace \cup
    \mathrm{Z}(\bar{g_{1}}, \ldots, \bar{g_{n}}).
\end{array}\]
\end{proof}

n40471.name: corollary_2
n40471.type_full:
∀ {F : Type u_5} [inst : Field F] [Fintype F] (n : Nat),
  GT.gt n 0 →
    ∀ (V : Type u_7) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : Module F V]
      (phi : LinearMap (RingHom.id F) V ((Fin n → F) → F)) (S : Set V),
      S.Finite →
        Exists fun T =>
          And T.Finite
            (And (LE.le T.ncard n)
              (And (Subset T ↑(Submodule.span F S)) (Eq (ZeroSet (Set.image (⇑phi) T)) (ZeroSet (Set.image (⇑phi) S)))))

n40472.name: corollary_3
n40472.type_full:
∀ {F : Type u_5} [inst : Field F] [Fintype F] (n : Nat) (V : Type u_7) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : Module F V]
  (phi : LinearMap (RingHom.id F) V (Projectivization F (Fin (HAdd.hAdd n 1) → F) → F)) (S : Set V),
  S.Finite →
    Ne (ZeroSet (Set.image (⇑phi) S)) EmptyCollection.emptyCollection →
      Exists fun T =>
        And T.Finite
          (And (LE.le T.ncard n)
            (And (Subset T ↑(Submodule.span F S)) (Eq (ZeroSet (Set.image (⇑phi) T)) (ZeroSet (Set.image (⇑phi) S)))))

n40473.name: matrix_rank_lemma
n40473.type_full:
∀ {F : Type u_5} [inst : Field F] [Fintype F] (n m : Nat),
  LE.le n m → ∀ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) F), Exists fun B => Exists fun M => And (Eq M.rank n) (Eq A (HMul.hMul B M))

n40474.name: prop_1
n40474.type_full:
∀ {F : Type u_5} [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : Fintype F] (n : Nat),
  GT.gt n 0 →
    Exists fun X =>
      Exists fun f =>
        And
          (Eq X.ncard
            (HAdd.hAdd
              (HDiv.hDiv (HSub.hSub (HPow.hPow (Fintype.card F) (HAdd.hAdd n 1)) (Fintype.card F))
                (HSub.hSub (Fintype.card F) 1))
              1))
          (And (∀ (x : ↑X), Exists fun i => Ne (f i x) 0)
            (∀ (g : Fin n → ↑X → F),
              (∀ (j : Fin n), Membership.mem (Submodule.span F (Set.range f)) (g j)) →
                Exists fun x => ∀ (j : Fin n), Eq (g j x) 0))

n40475.name: remark_example
n40475.type_full:
∀ {F : Type u_5} [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : Fintype F] (n : Nat),
  GT.gt n 0 →
    have f := fun i x => x i;
    And (Eq (ZeroSet (Set.range f)) (singleton 0))
      (∀ (g : Fin (HSub.hSub n 1) → (Fin n → F) → F),
        (∀ (j : Fin (HSub.hSub n 1)), Membership.mem (Submodule.span F (Set.range f)) (g j)) →
          GE.ge (ZeroSet (Set.range g)).ncard (Fintype.card F))

n40476.name: theorem_1
n40476.type_full:
∀ {F : Type u_5} [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : Fintype F] {X : Type u_6} [Finite X] [Finite X] (n : Nat) (S : Set (X → F)),
  S.Finite →
    GT.gt S.ncard n →
      LE.le (Nat.card X)
          (HDiv.hDiv (HSub.hSub (HPow.hPow (Fintype.card F) (HAdd.hAdd n 1)) (Fintype.card F))
            (HSub.hSub (Fintype.card F) 1)) →
        Exists fun T =>
          And (Subset T ↑(Submodule.span F S)) (And T.Finite (And (LE.le T.ncard n) (Eq (ZeroSet T) (ZeroSet S))))

n40477.name: theorem_1_aux
n40477.type_full:
∀ {F : Type u_5} [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : Fintype F] {X : Type u_6} [Finite X] (n : Nat)
  (f : X → Fin (HAdd.hAdd n 1) → F),
  LE.le (Nat.card X)
      (HDiv.hDiv (HSub.hSub (HPow.hPow (Fintype.card F) (HAdd.hAdd n 1)) (Fintype.card F))
        (HSub.hSub (Fintype.card F) 1)) →
    Exists fun M => Eq (setOf fun x => Eq (M (f x)) 0) (setOf fun x => Eq (f x) 0)
